text.p: Pharmaceuticals group Synthelabo said on Tuesday its growth targets for the rest of the decade were based on L'Oreal continuing to hold a majority in its capital.

"The plans that we envisage are similar to those put in place in 1991 and 1992, which have already allowed a change in the group's size, while L'Oreal maintained majority control," Synthelabo chairman Herve Gurein told analysts.
"I don't know what L'Oreal will do but I am confident," he added. L'Oreal held 56.64 percent of Synthelabo at the end of 1996.
L'Oreal chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones said on March 24 the company was constantly studying whether Synthelabo could develop on its own in the long run or needed an alliance.
Synthelabo earlier forecast a 10 percent increase in 1997 turnover and bigger rise in net earnings per share.

It confirmed a 19.7 percent increase in 1996 net attributable profits to 950.7 million francs and estimated net earnings per share would rise by 15-20 percent a year by 2000. It expected turnover of between 18-20 billion francs by the end of the decade.
